US-119-S3618.description: A bill to require the Federal Trade Commission to submit to Congress a report on the ability of minors to access fentanyl through social media platforms, and for other purposes.
US-119-S3618.aiSummary: The bill would require the Federal Trade Commission, working with federal health and drug agencies, to report to Congress on how minors can access fentanyl through social media platforms. The report would cover how sellers use these platforms, the risks to minors, how platform design may affect access, and what steps platforms and others have taken. It would also include recommendations for Congress and would be made public within 1 year after enactment.

US-119-HJRES203.title: Directing the Federal Trade Commission to investigate and report on anticompetitive practices and violations of the antitrust laws in the fire truck manufacturing industry.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HJRES203.aiSummary: The resolution would direct the Federal Trade Commission to investigate possible antitrust problems in the fire truck manufacturing industry and report back to Congress within 1 year after adoption. The report would cover things like price fixing, serial acquisitions, and monopolization, plus the effects on fire fighters, fire departments, states, towns, and small businesses. It would also ask for ideas for new laws or other fixes.

US-119-HJRES104.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "Miles City Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment".
US-119-HJRES104.summary: This joint resolution opens certain land administered by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) in eastern Montana to coal leasing. Specifically, it nullifies the rule issued by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan (RMP) Amendment for the Miles City Field Office in Montana. The BLM approved the RMP Amendment on November 20, 2024. The RMP Amendment made no acres available for coal leasing and 1,745,040 acres unavailable for further consideration for coal leasing to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
